text.p: The Malta government said on Tuesday its revenue in the first quarter of the year dropped by 15.8 million Malta pounds ($40.7 million) compared to January-March last year to reach 97.5 million pounds.
Recurrent expenditure and public debt servicing dropped by 5.7 million pounds to 115.2 million pounds in the same period, and capital expenditure fell by 4.6 million pounds to 13 million pounds.

The figures, carried in the comparative return of expenditure, showed that the drop in revenue was steepest from the Central Bank, down by 8.1 million pounds, and income tax, down by 4.7 million pounds.
Revenue from Value Added Tax rose by just over 3.5 million to 16.6 million, by far the biggest increase in revenue from all sources.
